title: Climate and Nature-Related Financial Risks
summary: How physical and transition risks arising from climate change and nature loss reach firms' balance sheets and business models, and the transmission channels supervisors need to understand.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How physical and transition risks arising from climate change and nature loss reach firms' balance sheets and business models, and the transmission channels supervisors need to understand.
Learning Objectives: Explain physical and transition risk and their transmission channels
Analyse sector and portfolio exposures to climate and nature-related risk
Assess the time horizon and uncertainty challenges in measuring these risks
Syllabus: Physical risk: acute and chronic hazards
Transition risk: policy, technology, market and litigation drivers
NGFS, Basel Committee and IAIS work on climate-related financial risk
Intended Audience: Supervisors and inspectors in banking, insurance, investment funds, investment services and pensions
Sustainable finance, policy and risk specialists supporting supervisory teams
Authorisation and product teams reviewing sustainability-related products and disclosures
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial supervision or risk assessment is helpful. No prior knowledge of sustainable finance or ESG is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Principles for the Effective Management and Supervision of Climate-related Financial Risks (2022)
NGFS, Guide for Supervisors: Integrating Climate-related and Environmental Risks into Prudential Supervision (2020)
ISSB, IFRS S1 General Requirements and IFRS S2 Climate-related Disclosures (2023)
IOSCO, Recommendations on Sustainability-Related Practices, Policies, Procedures and Disclosure in Asset Management (2021)
